detail: <p>Just after 4:00 PM this evening the Vancouver Fire Department was dispatched to reports of a house fire at 3000 NE 45th street in Vancouver. First arriving crews found a single story house with a large volume of fire and smoke coming from the back of the house. The fire appeared to have spread to the attic so firefighters went inside of the house with a hoseline to extinguish the fire. More firefighters climbed up a ladder to cut holes in the roof using chainsaws to ventilate the hose and let the hot smoke and gases out through the roof. It took 25 minutes to get the fire under control. An electrical line on the side of the house fell to the ground causing a brief safety concern but Clark PUD arrived swiftly to turn off the power to the home. 3 occupants and a pet were able to escape safely without injury and denied the assistance of red cross. In total, 22 firefighters were on scene. Firefighters are still on scene performing overhaul and ensuring that all hot spots are fully extinguished. No other injuries were reported. The cause of the fire is under investigation by the Vancouver Fire Marshal's Office.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="text-align: center;"><span style="font-size:20px"><strong>Oregon Private Job Vacancies Flatten Out in 2025</strong></span></p>

<p style="text-align: center;">&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>SALEM, Ore.</strong>&nbsp;—&nbsp;Oregon private employers reported 58,500 job openings at any given time in 2025. This was essentially unchanged from the 57,800 job openings seen in 2024, according to new data from the Oregon Employment Department’s Job Vacancy Survey.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>In research published today, senior research analyst Anna Johnson reports that the health care and social assistance industry saw the strongest level of hiring in 2025, with over a quarter of all vacancies coming from companies in that sector. Most job openings across the state tended to be for full-time and permanent positions. Vacancies with higher education requirements also had a greater likelihood for prior experience requirements, and higher average wages.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>Oregon saw record high levels of job vacancies in the recovery from the pandemic recession in 2021 and 2022. Vacancies returned to pre-pandemic levels in 2024 and 2025. For the full analysis, see the article <a href="https://qualityinfo.org/-/oregon-private-job-vacancies-2025-job-vacancies-remained-flat">Oregon Private Job Vacancies: 2025 Job Vacancies Remained Flat</a>.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>About Workforce and Economic Research</strong></p>

<p>The Workforce and Economic Research Division of the Oregon Employment Department develops and distributes quality economic and workforce information to help Oregonians make informed decisions and support a thriving economy. Staff collect data from state and federal records and surveys; analyze the available information; and share insights with the public in a variety of ways, including regular reports, publications, and the website, <a href="https://www.qualityinfo.org/" target="_blank" title="https://www.qualityinfo.org/">QualityInfo.org</a>.</p>

<p><strong>Media Contact:</strong>&nbsp; <a href="mailto:Communications@employ.oregon.gov">Communications@employ.oregon.gov</a></p>

<p><strong>Governor Tina Kotek Press Office: </strong><a href="mailto:governors.press@oregon.gov">governors.press@oregon.gov</a></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><strong><span style="font-size:20px">Employment Department Shares Plan to Improve Customer Service and Strengthen Oregon’s Workforce System</span></strong></p>

<p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:16px">The agency outlines 101 prioritized actions and long-term initiatives, many already underway</span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>SALEM, Ore</strong>. —&nbsp; The Oregon Employment Department (OED) has released a comprehensive report on its ongoing effort to improve customer service and strengthen Oregon’s public workforce system. The action plan meets <a href="https://www-auth.oregon.gov/employ/Agency/Documents/2025/2025.06.23_StolfiAgencyExpectationsGovernorsLetter.pdf">expectations outlined by Governor Tina Kotek</a> and demonstrates progress already underway under Director Andrew R. Stolfi.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“Oregonians deserve the best customer service we can provide to make sure they have what they need, especially in times of employment transition,” Governor Tina Kotek said. “The department is taking these issues head on, and the action areas identified in the director’s report will help get us there.”</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>At the Governor’s direction, OED conducted a review of the customer experience across Unemployment Insurance (UI), Paid Leave Oregon (Paid Leave), Contributions &amp; Recovery (C&amp;R), WorkSource Oregon (WSO), and the Frances Online system. The resulting <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Agency/Pages/Customer-Service-Workforce-Strategies-Action-Plan-.aspx">Customer Service and Workforce Strategies Action Plan</a>&nbsp;includes&nbsp;a prioritized list of 101 customer-focused action steps that fall into four main categories:</p>

<ul>
     <li>Customer service improvements</li>
     <li>Organizational improvements</li>
     <li>Improvements to Frances Online</li>
     <li>Improvements to the public workforce system</li>
</ul>

<p>The actions range from high-impact, short-term initiatives to long-term system changes, with the following projects as the highest, most immediate priorities:</p>

<ul>
     <li>Use AI-assisted tools to improve customer service and employee workflows for faster resolution of common and complex issues.</li>
     <li>Review and simplify all customer-facing communications so customers better understand OED’s processes and can more easily receive benefits.</li>
     <li>Equip WorkSource Oregon centers with additional tools to help customers navigate UI claims.</li>
     <li>Improve how the agency collects and analyzes data to support well-informed goal setting, process improvement, and accountability.</li>
     <li>Create an online live claim status tracker so customers know where they are and what to expect at each step of the process for Paid Leave Oregon and UI.</li>
     <li>Consolidate Title I and Title III Workforce Innovation Opportunity Act (WIOA) administration and funding within OED to improve efficiency and accountability within Oregon’s public workforce system.</li>
</ul>

<p>“This action plan reflects OED’s deep commitment to improving the services we provide,” OED Director Andrew R. Stolfi said. “It draws from our strengths and is centered on the customer experience, which is where our focus will remain.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>When Stolfi joined OED as director, the Governor asked him to lead a thorough review of the agency and develop a comprehensive plan to improve customer service and advance OED’s workforce development mission. In pursuing this directive, OED gathered extensive feedback from across the state through surveys, focus groups, and interviews with more than 5,000 customers, 850 employees, and 240 frontline staff. That feedback revealed clear, consistent themes across programs and communities, including the need for clearer, faster, and more predictable service for Paid Leave and UI customers, and simpler processes and clearer guidance for employers that engage with OED’s business services.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“Our goal was to identify what is working, where barriers exist, and what improvements will make the greatest difference for the people and businesses we serve,” said Director Stolfi. “You can draw a direct line between the feedback we received and the actions outlined in this plan.”</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>A <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Agency/Pages/Customer-Service-Workforce-Strategies-Action-Plan-.aspx">plan summary</a>, a <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Agency/Pages/Prioritized-Projects.aspx">categorized list of prioritized actions</a>, and the <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Agency/Documents/2026/2026.OED-Customer-Service-Workforce-Strategies-Action-plan-FINAL.pdf">full action plan</a> are available on the <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Pages/default.aspx">OED website</a>. OED will continue to share progress updates and engage with customers, partners, and the public as we move forward.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“We’ve already started working on many of these projects, and Oregonians should expect to see many changes and improvements in the coming months,” Stolfi said. “Customer service is our top priority, and we will not rest until every Oregonian gets the services they expect in a timely manner.”</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>The agency has already improved in some key customer service metrics. For example, from July 2025 through January 2026 in Unemployment Insurance, the average time to answer a call was 22 minutes faster than the same seven-month period the prior year, despite a 13.6 percent increase in initial claims filed. The Paid Leave program has also reduced the average time it takes for staff to decide on a claim by 5.8 days, despite a 17.6 percent increase in application volume. This indicates improvements in operational efficiency, even while more Oregonians are using these programs.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“We are encouraged by the progress we’ve already made but recognize that we must continue improving in order to provide the level of customer service Oregonians deserve,” Stolfi said. “This plan lays out exactly how we’ll do that.”</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>About the Oregon Employment Department</strong></p>

<p>The Oregon Employment Department (OED) provides economic stability to Oregon communities by providing vital services to both businesses and workers.&nbsp; OED supports businesses with finding qualified job candidates, labor market information, tax incentives and support, and retaining talent through economic downturns. OED promotes employment through wage replacement benefits during unemployment and significant life events, job placement, training, and useful career information. Learn more at <a href="https://www.oregon.gov/employ/Pages/default.aspx">employment.oregon.gov.</a></p>

The cause of the fire is under investigation by the Vancouver Fire Marshal’s Office.&nbsp;</p>

</div>

<div class="OutlineElement Ltr SCXW15318782 BCX0" style="-webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; clear: both; cursor: text; overflow: visible; position: relative; direction: ltr; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web&quot;, Arial, Verdana, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">

<div class="OutlineElement Ltr SCXW15318782 BCX0" style="-webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; clear: both; cursor: text; overflow: visible; position: relative; direction: ltr; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web&quot;, Arial, Verdana, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">
<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><strong>Portland, OR — March 11, 2026&nbsp;</strong></span></span><strong><span style="font-size:16px">—</span></strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif"><span style="font-size:16px">The&nbsp;Black Business Association of Oregon (BBAO)&nbsp;has&nbsp;released its&nbsp;<strong><a href="https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__drive.google.com_file_d_1zCEDPY6dYhn4bcrRa0q2jc1C-2DbvNR5FK_view-3Fusp-3Dsharing&amp;d=DwMGaQ&amp;c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&amp;r=Ib9MeinY34Npk1XLeNcxht0Jk5GecACzbs_p3kN6t_s&amp;m=ZMXYafUt9WGGE1oLV4QGRGf0nFHa87rZGdn6wp8R5OxDbs44mdnc55j4ENdoO5jH&amp;s=4ShaRSAXPhSqnu7Fh0Ij2DsMGU-YMwrvIq4QDnM9Yeg&amp;e=">Strategic Roadmap</a>,</strong>&nbsp;which will guide coordinated legislative advocacy&nbsp;across Black-focused organizations, public agencies, corporations, and philanthropic partners.<span style="background-color:transparent">&nbsp;Informed by data analyses conducted by&nbsp;ECOnorthwest,&nbsp;facilitated&nbsp;by Interplay Collective, and led by BBAO,&nbsp;the Roadmap provides&nbsp;an&nbsp;</span><strong>action-oriented framework</strong>&nbsp;to&nbsp;address systemic drivers of inequity in Black business outcomes.</span></span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">The Roadmap outlines&nbsp;</span><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">seven phases&nbsp;of action&nbsp;from January 2026&nbsp;to January&nbsp;2027,&nbsp;</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">including&nbsp;developing&nbsp;coalitions, drafting&nbsp;policy goals and legislative recommendations,&nbsp;convening&nbsp;stakeholders,&nbsp;and&nbsp;releasing a State of the Black Economy Report.&nbsp;Ahead of the 2027 legislative&nbsp;session,&nbsp;BBAO seeks to introduce a&nbsp;</span><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">full legislative package</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">&nbsp;to&nbsp;improve Black business participation, scale, and long-term economic stability.&nbsp;</span></p>
</div>

<div class="OutlineElement Ltr SCXW15318782 BCX0" style="-webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; clear: both; cursor: text; overflow: visible; position: relative; direction: ltr; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web&quot;, Arial, Verdana, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">
<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif"><span style="font-size:16px"><span style="background-color:transparent">Partners from&nbsp;a number of&nbsp;Oregon organizations, including&nbsp;both private organizations&nbsp;and public agencies, contributed to the Roadmap.</span>&nbsp;</span></span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">Nate McCoy, Interim Executive Director of BBAO and the President and CEO of&nbsp;the National Association of Minority Contractors of Oregon (NAMC-Oregon)</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">, said, “BBAO’s Strategic Roadmap is designed to move from conversation to coordinated&nbsp;action. It&nbsp;is not another&nbsp;report,&nbsp;it is an implementation framework that aligns policy, partners, community leadership, and intentional access to capital to accelerate Black business growth and wealth creation across Oregon.”&nbsp;</span></p>
</div>

<div class="OutlineElement Ltr SCXW15318782 BCX0" style="-webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; clear: both; cursor: text; overflow: visible; position: relative; direction: ltr; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web&quot;, Arial, Verdana, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">
<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">Alando Simpson,&nbsp;Board Chair of BBAO and CEO of&nbsp;COR Disposal &amp; Recycling</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">, added,&nbsp;“BBAO works&nbsp;to&nbsp;build an economy where Black-owned businesses can thrive.&nbsp;This Strategic Roadmap&nbsp;will&nbsp;support BBAO and partners in&nbsp;aligning policy, capital, and accountability mechanisms&nbsp;to cultivate a thriving and&nbsp;equitable&nbsp;business ecosystem&nbsp;where&nbsp;Oregon’s Black-owned&nbsp;businesses&nbsp;can&nbsp;achieve sustainable growth and prosperity.”&nbsp;</span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">Andrew Hoan, President and CEO of the Portland Metro Chamber and a Board Member of BBAO,&nbsp;</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">added, “BBAO is leading the way in advancing economic equity in&nbsp;Oregon.&nbsp;The launch of this Strategic Roadmap&nbsp;represents&nbsp;the continued commitment of BBAO&nbsp;and partners&nbsp;to&nbsp;coordinated,&nbsp;focused advocacy&nbsp;for&nbsp;the&nbsp;expansion of&nbsp;business opportunities&nbsp;among&nbsp;Black Oregonians.&nbsp;The Portland Metro Chamber is in full&nbsp;support&nbsp;of&nbsp;BBAO’s advocacy for the&nbsp;Black business community.”&nbsp; &nbsp;</span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">BBAO&nbsp;emerged&nbsp;from a moment of national reckoning and has grown into a data-informed, policy-focused statewide champion for Black economic parity.&nbsp;In 2020, Black leaders on the Portland Metro Chamber board published the&nbsp;</span><a class="Hyperlink SCXW15318782 BCX0" href="https://portlandmetrochamber.com/policy/black-economic-prosperity/" rel="noreferrer noopener" style="font-size: 16px; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; -webkit-user-drag: none; -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; user-select: text; text-decoration-line: none;" target="_blank"><strong>Regional Black Economic Prosperity Agenda</strong></a><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">,</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">&nbsp;which&nbsp;laid&nbsp;the groundwork for the establishment of BBAO.</span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">BBAO was officially launched in 2022 through a collaboration between the&nbsp;</span><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">Portland Metro Chamber</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">&nbsp;and&nbsp;</span><strong style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">NAMC-Oregon</strong><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">, with&nbsp;nearly $1 million&nbsp;in&nbsp;initial&nbsp;public, private, and philanthropic funding.&nbsp;With strong leadership and deep partnerships with the broader business community, BBAO builds political power and expands economic opportunity for Black communities in Oregon.&nbsp;</span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">Black-owned businesses are essential drivers of Oregon’s economy, community stability, and cultural vitality. Yet their contributions have long been constrained by structural barriers, including inequitable access to capital, contracting, and workforce pipelines, as well as public and private systems not designed to support Black entrepreneurs at scale. Despite these challenges, Black business owners across Oregon continue to lead with resilience, innovation, and vision.&nbsp;</span></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif; font-size:16px">BBAO’s Strategic Roadmap will strengthen cross-sector&nbsp;accountability and&nbsp;help shape policies and partnerships that advance&nbsp;equitable&nbsp;economic outcomes for Black Oregonians, and for Oregon as a whole.&nbsp;</span></p>
</div>

<h1 style="text-align:center"><span style="font-family:arial,helvetica,sans-serif"><strong>WorkSource Oregon Invites Job Seekers to Job Fair for Autistic Community Activity Program</strong></span></h1>

<p><strong>OREGON CITY, Ore.</strong>&nbsp;– WorkSource Oregon invites job seekers to a job fair with the Autistic Community Activity Program (ACAP) on Wednesday, March 18,10 a.m. to 1 p.m., at the WorkSource center in Oregon City. This is an opportunity to learn about summer jobs in the Portland-Metro area to help people with autism build lasting life skills. ACAP staff will be on site to share more information and conduct interviews for one-on-one assistants with their summer program. There is no cost to attend, and participants are encouraged to bring their resumes.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>“Are you looking for the most fun you’ve ever had in a summer job? Come work with ACAP in an active and engaging environment where you get to meet new people and make friends,” said Brooke Pyper, chief operating officer at ACAP. “This allows you to serve the community, explore Portland, and help autistic individuals build lasting life skills. You will work in groups, travel around the city, enjoy the sun, and engage with clients to ensure their goals are met.”</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

<p>Assistants will earn $18 to $23 per hour during ACAP’s 2026 summer season, which runs from June through August. Internships and work-study hours are also available.</p>

<p>“WorkSource Oregon is excited to support job seekers as they explore a wide range of employment opportunities — from seasonal positions to roles that make a meaningful impact in their communities,” said Jim Pfarrer, director of Workforce Operations with the Oregon Employment Department. “The ACAP Job Fair is a great example of that commitment, and an opportunity for job seekers to make a strong impression. headline: (Update)Gas leak with restricted areas in Vancouver (Photos) (Photo)
detail: <p>At 10:22 this morning the Vancouver Fire Department was dispatched to the area of 6000 NE 60th avenue for the report of a broken natural gas line after a third party contractor was digging in the area and accidentally damaged the 2 inch line. Firefighters found a heavy smell of natural gas in the area and about 20 homes that required evacuation. The VFD had 3 fire apparatus on scene along with a battalion chief to isolate the area and continue air monitoring. Reverse 911 phone calls were sent out to surrounding neighborhoods advising them of the potential hazard. Firefighters were blocking access at NE 59th circle and NE 59th avenue, NE 62nd street and NE 59th avenue and NE 60th avenue and NE 62nd street. NWNG arrived on scene and mitigated the broken natural gas line. CTRAN provided assistance by bringing a bus to the area to shelter those who evacuated their homes. This area has now been deemed safe for entry and all firefighters have cleared the scene and citizens are clear to return to their homes.&nbsp;</p>
